results.content:
#### ***The major release integrates ACORD quoting, carrier-registered telephony, owned email deliverability, and pre-built workflows into one autonomous platform.***  
*The major release integrates ACORD quoting, carrier-registered telephony, owned email deliverability, and pre-built workflows into one autonomous platform.*  
[SUPERAGENT AI,](https://getsuperagent.com/) Inc. today announced the general availability of SUPERAGENT 2.0, a comprehensive platform update that transitions the software from an AI feature set into a unified autonomous workforce for independent insurance agencies.  
Developed over the first quarter of 2026, the 2.0 release encompasses over 2,600 updates and introduces five core infrastructure pillars: unified AI agents, managed telephony, automated email deliverability, real-time quoting, and enterprise-grade security.  
“With SUPERAGENT 2.0, we are shifting from providing a standalone AI tool to delivering a complete, autonomous workforce platform,” said Vlada Lotkina, CEO of SUPERAGENT AI. “Agencies no longer need to bolt AI onto legacy systems. They can now provision compliant phone numbers, warm email domains, and deploy autonomous quoting capabilities within a single, unified environment.”  
**Read More on Fintech:[Global Fintech Interview with Baran Ozkan, co-founder & CEO of Flagright](https://globalfintechseries.com/interviews/global-fintech-interview-with-baran-ozkan-co-founder-ceo-of-flagright/)**  
The Five Pillars of SUPERAGENT 2.0
The Five Pillars of SUPERAGENT 2.0  
The release consolidates multiple disparate agency tools into a single ecosystem, featuring:  
- Unified AI Agents & Quality Scoring: The platform introduces a universal AI architecture that handles inbound routing, outbound campaigns, renewals, and training. Every conversation, whether handled by AI or a human agent, is now graded using a new FICO-inspired Quality Score engine (300-850), evaluating eight core competencies including discovery, rapport, and objection handling. The AI also features automatic cross-sell detection to identify revenue opportunities during service calls.
- Real-Time ACORD Quoting: The AI agents can now generate bound-ready ACORD 80 (Homeowners) and ACORD 90 (Auto) applications directly from phone conversations. Utilizing integrations with EZLynx and other API, the system applies state-specific underwriting logic and validates data in real-time, reducing manual data entry.
- Managed Telephony & Carrier Trust: Agencies can now purchase and provision phone numbers directly within the platform. The system automatically manages Twilio A2P brand registration and implements A-level SHAKEN/STIR attestation, ensuring outbound calls display as verified to consumers.
- Email Deliverability Suite: The update includes one-click domain provisioning, automated sender warming, and dedicated campaign inboxes with threaded reply handling. The platform enforces strict communication compliance, natively integrating CAN-SPAM, TCPA quiet hours, and Do-Not-Call (DNC) scrubbing into every workflow.
- Battle-Tested Revenue Workflows: The platform comes equipped with pre-built workflows and message templates engineered for every revenue-generating scenario. Agencies can instantly deploy automated sequences for everything from speed-to-lead and cold lead outreach to win-backs, cross-sells, and policy renewals without building campaigns from scratch.  
Industry Impact and Adoption:  
Early adopters of the 2.0 architecture report significant operational consolidations, utilizing the platform to replace disparate dialers, training simulators, and quoting assistants.  
“SUPERAGENT 2.0 allows me to focus my communication efforts with clients and prospects on money-generating activities,” said Andrew McGinnis, owner of McGinnis Insurance Services. “The AI agents allow us to increase our inbound and outbound communications without adding hours to my team’s day, giving them the ability to focus on tasks that directly drive our agency’s growth.”

results.name: Changelog - Product Updates | Superagent
results.content:
August 15, 2026
## Context Guardrails for everything agents consume  
Score web pages, email, files, agent skills, and public GitHub MCP repositories before an agent trusts them.  
Runtime Guardrails decide what an agent may do. Context Guardrails decide what an agent may consume.  
Agents fetch pages, open files, install skills, and connect MCP servers without reviewing any of it. Superagent now scores that untrusted context first, so agents keep full capability without inheriting hostile input.
### Five origins, available now  
- **Web pages**— domain identity, redirect chains, hidden DOM, and rendered page text. New lookups return a preliminary identity score immediately and finish the deep scan in the background.
- **Email**— sender authentication, phishing and injection patterns, attachments, and outbound links.
- **Files**— public text and PDFs, with type consistency, encoded instructions, and prompt injection checks. File bytes are never stored.
- **Agent skills**— GitHub publisher identity, requested capabilities, hidden instructions, and install hooks. Skill files are treated as untrusted data and are never executed.
- **MCP repositories**— static review of public GitHub MCP servers, including tool descriptions, schemas, instructions, hooks, and secrets. Superagent never connects to a live MCP endpoint or runs the server.  
Full repositories remain covered by [repository red teaming](https://www.superagent.sh/docs/red-team/repository-reports). Packages remain covered by [supply-chain scanning](https://www.superagent.sh/docs/pr-scans/supply-chain-scanning).

results.title: Changelog - Product Updates | Superagent
results.snippet: August 15, 2026 ## Context Guardrails for everything agents consume Score web pages, email, files, agent skills, and public GitHub MCP repositories before an agent trusts them. Runtime Guardrails decide what an agent may do. Context Guardrails decide what an agent may consume. Agents fetch pages, open files, install skills, and connect MCP servers without reviewing any of it. Superagent now scores that untrusted context first, so agents keep full capability without inheriting hostile input. ### Five origins, available now - **Web pages**— domain identity, redirect chains, hidden DOM, and rendered page text. New lookups return a preliminary identity score immediately and finish the deep scan in the background. - **Email**— sender authentication, phishing and injection patterns, attachments, and outbound links. - **Files**— public text and PDFs, with type consistency, encoded instructions, and prompt injection checks. File bytes are never stored. - **Agent skills**— GitHub publisher identity, requested capabilities, hidden instructions, and install hooks. Skill files are treated as untrusted data and are never executed. - **MCP repositories**— static review of public GitHub MCP serve
